These energies are written in terms of double integrals accounting for pairwise interactions in an open set $\Omega$, weighted by a kernel $K_\varepsilon$. If the latter is controlled from above and below by suitable non-negative radial kernels with unit mass concentrating at the origin, then, up to subsequences, the $\Gamma$-limit has domain $BV(\Omega;Y)$ and is given by a local surface energy. We show that the locality of the $\Gamma$-limit is not guaranteed if the concentration of mass fails. For a class of reference energies, we obtain a more explicit representation of the limit energy, also for non-radial kernels, recovering the limits of isotropic and anisotropic fractional perimeters. We also prove a homogenization result for periodic kernels.

papers.title: Minimum-Area Enclosing Rectangles and the First Neumann Eigenvalue of Planar Convex Domains
papers.authors: Xiaolong Li, Jin Sun, Kui Wang
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in the plane and let $R$ be a minimum-area rectangle containing $\overline\Omega$. We prove that if the ratio of the shorter side of $R$ to its longer side is at most $\rho \approx 0.443485$, then the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue of $\Omega$ is bounded from below by that of $R$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ coincides with the interior of $R$. The proof is based on a flux identity for the means of a test function over vertical sections of $\Omega$, combined with weighted estimates involving the distributional second derivatives of the boundary functions. Finally, we show that the threshold $\rho\approx0.443485$ is nearly optimal by constructing, for every ratio in $(0.457994,1/2)$, trapezoids that are arbitrarily close to their minimum-area enclosing rectangle and for which the inequality fails.

papers.title: Reconnection in 2D Inertial Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.authors: Lydia Boubendir, Peter Constantin, Hezekiah Grayer II, Zhongtian Hu
papers.abstract: We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. We finally show numerical examples of magnetic reconnection, validating known rigorous results and uncovering new cases.

papers.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

papers.title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
papers.abstract:
We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $\mu_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^\alpha}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $\nu_t$ and its linear evolution $\mu_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $\nu_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant.
  We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $\mu_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t \Delta} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.

papers.title: Faber--Krahn inequality for homogeneous normalized $p$-Laplacian type operators
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the normalized (or game-theoretic) $p$-Laplacian, proving that, for $p\geq 2$, the ball uniquely minimizes the principal Dirichlet eigenvalue among bounded connected Lipschitz domains of prescribed volume satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition. More generally, we prove the same inequality for the family of homogeneous operators $|Du|^\gamma\Delta_p^N u$, with $p>1$ and $-1<\gamma\le p-2$. Unlike the classical $p$-Laplacian, these operators lack a variational structure, preventing the use of standard symmetrization arguments. Our proof overcomes this difficulty through a level-set approach: it relies on a flux identity for the eigenvalue, for which a variational interpretation re-emerges in the special case where the domain is a ball.

papers.title: Sharp maximum estimates for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients
papers.authors: Shibing Chen, Neil S. Trudinger, Xu-Jia Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper we obtain sharp exponents in the Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci maximum estimate for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients, originally conjectured by Pucci in 1966 \cite{Pucci}, together with corresponding sharp results under the more natural quantification of uniform ellipticity in more than two dimensions. The proofs combine a Hessian integral inequality obtained from boundary Morse inequalities with an obstacle argument. The estimates also hold on arbitrary open sets, of finite volume, without regularity assumptions on their boundaries.

papers.title: Cavity collapse and kinetic energy concentration in three-dimensional free-boundary Euler flow
papers.abstract: We construct smooth axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations in bounded domains for which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at a finite time $T$. The velocity has a single-valued potential, and the construction applies without surface tension and with any fixed positive surface tension. Both boundary components remain embedded and disjoint before collapse, while the outer boundary converges smoothly. The terminal outer meridional domain may be any smooth bounded simply connected domain whose closure is separated from the rotation axis; the interior point generating the collapse circle and the positive concentrated energy may be prescribed independently. We prove a sharp collapse law with radius asymptotic to an explicit multiple of $(T-t)^{1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{-1/4}$, determine curvature blow-up asymptotics, and show that kinetic energy concentrates uniformly on the circle. For a canonical reflection symmetric family, we identify a common cylindrical spacetime limit and sharp velocity and pressure profiles. At every fixed spatial point in the region enclosed by the limiting outer boundary and away from the collapse circle, the velocity tends to zero while the pressure tends to positive infinity. For this family, we characterize the topology of the limiting material map and prove its optimal $1/2$-H\"older regularity and sharp $W^{1,p}$ threshold $1\le p<2$, with first derivatives in weak $L^2$ but not in $L^2$. These canonical solutions admit weak continuations that preserve mass and momentum and whose total energy drops at collapse by exactly the concentrated kinetic energy.

papers.title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract:
This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*}
  u_t-|Du|^\gamma F(D^2u)=f
  \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ \gamma>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (\lambda, \Lambda)$-elliptic with $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\alpha)>0 $ such that \[
  |\gamma|+\left(\frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}-1\right) \leq \varepsilon
  \quad \Longrightarrow \quad
  u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (\gamma, \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.

papers.title: Dissipative solutions for fibred Wasserstein gradient flows of Cahn-Hilliard-type energies
papers.authors: Georg Heinze, Katharina Hopf, Matthias Liero
papers.abstract: We study fourth-order evolution equations with a fibred Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, describing spatial transport of finitely many or a continuum of types. The driving Cahn-Hilliard-like energy combines a diagonal gradient contribution with nonlinear interactions between types. We prove subsequential convergence of the fibred Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme to solutions satisfying an energy-dissipation inequality. For general type distributions, the absence of compactness in the type variable is addressed through defect-based solution concepts. On $\mathbb R^d, d\le 3$, we construct dissipative solutions satisfying an additional entropy-dissipation inequality. On smooth bounded domains in any space dimension, a coercivity estimate for the metric slope allows us to construct energy-dissipating solutions without relying on flow interchange, thereby covering non-convex domains endowed with the intrinsic length distance. In both cases, a variational comparison of the piecewise constant and De Giorgi interpolants yields a common limiting energy and strong convergence of the difference to zero without requiring strong compactness. For finitely many types, the defects vanish and the construction yields weak solutions. We further establish weak-strong uniqueness of dissipative solutions in every space dimension and of energy-dissipating solutions in dimensions $d\le5$. Combined with the respective existence results, this yields strong convergence of the variational approximations whenever a sufficiently regular, strictly positive solution exists.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of a Bloch skyrmion for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of isolated skyrmions under the flow of the two-dimensional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. We consider a micromagnetic energy functional involving the exchange energy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and the Zeeman interaction. We are interested in the stability of chiral Bloch skyrmions, which are local minimizers of this energy. We prove that data in H2 which are near in the skyrmion in a slighlty stronger than H1 sense, converge with exponential rate, in H2, to the skyrmion, up to a change of gauge.

papers.title: Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods
papers.authors: Nilasis Chaudhuri, Piotr B. Mucha, Tomasz Piasecki, Jiakun Yang
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the conditional H\"older regularity of the temperature for the heat-conducting compressible Navier-Stokes system, where the pressure takes a complete form that includes the Stefan-radiation correction. Under minimal assumptions on the density and velocity, we prove that any weak solution automatically exhibits H\"older continuity in the temperature component. This constitutes the main result of the work and is achieved by an application of the De Giorgi method. As a consequence of this conditional regularity, we establish the global-in-time existence of a regular, unique solution to a simplified system for the compressible potential flow of a heat-conducting fluid, valid for arbitrarily large initial data.

papers.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing elastic particles
papers.abstract:
This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size.
  For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.

papers.title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
papers.authors: Mingxiang Li, Quoc Anh Ngo, Xingwang Xu
papers.abstract: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.

papers.title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
papers.authors: Rachel Morris, Ryan Murray, Kerrek Stinson
papers.abstract: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.

papers.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
papers.abstract: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.

papers.title: Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
papers.authors: Xuezhi Chen, Changxing Miao, Jiye Yuan, Tengfei Zhao
papers.abstract: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.

papers.title: Exponential convergence to a steady-state for a population genetics model with sexual reproduction and selection
papers.abstract: We are interested in the dynamics of a population structured by a phenotypic trait. Individuals reproduce sexually, which is represented by a non-linear integral operator. This operator is combined to a multiplicative operator representing selection. When the strength of selection is small, we show that the dynamics of the population is governed by a simple macroscopic differential equation, and that solutions converge exponentially to steady-states that are locally unique. The analysis is based on Wasserstein distance inequalities using a uniform lower bound on distributions. These inequalities are coupled to tail estimates to show the stability of the steady-states.

papers.title: Quantitative Schauder estimates for hypoelliptic equations
papers.abstract: We derive Schauder estimates using ideas from Campanato's approach for a general class of local hypoelliptic operators and non-local kinetic equations. The method covers equations in divergence and non-divergence form. In particular our results are applicable to the inhomogeneous Landau and to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation. The paper is self-contained.

papers.title: Scaling-Critical Theory for the Boltzmann and Landau Equations
papers.authors: Ke Chen, Quoc-Hung Nguyen, Tong Yang
papers.abstract:
This paper develops a scaling-critical theory for the spatially inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann and Landau equations with very soft potentials. For sufficiently small initial perturbations in a localized, weighted, anisotropic Riesz-potential norm, we prove global well-posedness near a Maxwellian in the whole space. This critical phase-space norm captures the Boltzmann--Landau scaling, the velocity-dependent anisotropy, and the hypoelliptic transport structure. The proof combines frozen-operator estimates, a critical fixed-point argument, and weighted hypocoercive energy estimates.
  We also develop a short-time pointwise Green-function theory for variable-coefficient kinetic equations with a nonnegative H\"older background. We first construct the small-jump Green function by freezing coefficients along kinetic characteristics and then recover the full kernel through a convergent parametrix expansion. The resulting bounds capture the fractional Kolmogorov geometry near characteristics and rapid decay away from them. These estimates form the analytic core of the scaling-critical theory and provide a robust pointwise framework for further regularity analysis in the soft-potential regime.

papers.title: Nonlinear effects of incoming time-periodic boundary conditions on shock waves for scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the large-time behavior of inviscid and viscous shocks for scalar conservation laws on the half-line $(-\infty,0)$ under an incoming \emph{time-periodic} boundary condition. This problem arises naturally from classical piston problems in fluid mechanics. Even for arbitrarily small periodic oscillations of the boundary data, the effect of the boundary manifests itself through a persistent time-periodic component near the boundary, which behaves as a \emph{boundary wave}.
  For inviscid shocks moving away from the boundary ($s<0$), this boundary wave repeatedly interacts with the shock over infinitely many periods. We show that the repeated interactions do not generate secular growth, but instead produce a finite \emph{cumulative} correction to the asymptotic shock location. For the inviscid stationary case $s=0$, the time-periodic boundary \emph{modulates} the background stationary shock into a genuinely time-periodic shock configuration, to which the solution converges. In the viscous case with $s<0$, the boundary wave couples with the viscous shock through a transitional region induced by diffusion, and the solution converges asymptotically to their superposition. Our results show that for scalar conservation laws, the persistent boundary wave modifies the shock without producing resonance.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for convex functions with periodic Monge-Amp\`ere measure
papers.authors: Tianling Jin, YanYan Li, Hung V. Tran, Xushan Tu
papers.abstract:
We study global convex solutions of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation \[ \det D^2 u = \mu \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n, \] where $\mu \not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite periodic Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove a Liouville-type theorem showing that every such solution admits a unique decomposition, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a quadratic polynomial and a periodic function. This extends earlier results of Caffarelli-Li and Li-Lu, which required $\mu$ to have a density with regular or bounded logarithm, to the full generality of periodic measures, allowing degeneracy and singularities. A key ingredient is a new dichotomous Harnack-type inequality for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations with nonnegative periodic measures, which compensates for the failure of doubling and engulfing properties in the degenerate setting.
  In the extremal example where $\mu$ is the periodic Dirac measure supported on the integer lattice, we show that the solutions, up to addition of a linear function, are in one-to-one correspondence with Dirichlet-Voronoi tilings of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Modal bases of coaxial electromagnetic step index fibers
papers.abstract: We consider the eigenvalue problem to find the modes of an electromagnetic coaxial step index fiber. More specific, we consider a closed (meaning PEC boundary conditions) cylindrical waveguide with circular cross section $\Gamma$, wave propagation modeled by the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations with frequency $\omega$, the permeability $\mu$ and the permittivity $\epsilon$ being scalar, uniformly positive, piece-wise constant and depending only on the radial variable of the cross section. We prove that if the deviation from the homogeneous case is small, i.e., $\delta_{\epsilon,\mu}:=\|\epsilon-\epsilon_0\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mu-\mu_0\|_{L^\infty}<<1$, then the (appropriately scaled) tangential electric (magnetic) fields of the modes form Riesz bases in $\mathbf{H}_{0}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$ ($\mathbf{H}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$) and the natural trace space $\mathbf{H}_{0}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$ ($\mathbf{H}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$). These results hold also for complex frequencies $\omega$. In addition, if $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$, then for small enough $\delta_{\epsilon,\mu}$ all wavenumbers are located on the axes and there exist no backward modes. Key tools in the analysis are a particular reformulation of the eigenvalue problem, the perturbation theory for selfadjoint operators under a local subordinate condition and uniform properties of Bessel functions.

papers.title: Non-Existence of thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers
papers.abstract: We examine the existence of thick bubble rings within the framework of the free-boundary capillary Euler equations, focusing on the regime of low Weber numbers. Although spheroidal bubbles are known to approach a spherical shape in this limit, the possibility of thick bubble rings persisting at low Weber numbers has remained uncertain. In contrast to the ordinary Euler equations, which admit thick vortex ring solutions, our analysis reveals that the free-boundary capillary Euler equations do not support thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers. This distinction highlights the significant impact of surface tension on the behavior of vortex rings in the capillary regime.

papers.title: Isolated Singularities for Fractional Hartree Equations
papers.authors: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang
papers.abstract:
We study isolated singularities of positive solutions to a fractional Hartree equation with Riesz interaction,
  \[
  (-\Delta)^s u
  =
  \left(
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}}
  \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}\,dy
  \right)u^q
  \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}.
  \]
  The puncture changes the passage from the differential equation to its integral form: a fractional fundamental solution term may occur at the singular point. Under an upper bound at the scale of the fundamental solution and a weighted integrability condition on the source, we derive a Riesz decomposition with a nonnegative singular term. Under the same assumptions, if in addition the solution blows up at the puncture, \(p,q\ge1\), and both Kelvin weights are nonnegative, an off-center moving spheres argument yields radial symmetry and strict radial decrease. We also classify positive radial homogeneous singular solutions under the corresponding convergence conditions. If a nonzero positive radial homogeneous scaling limit exists and solves the limiting equation, this classification uniquely determines its coefficient.

papers.title: Non-radial solutions for the quasi-linear H\'enon type $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation
papers.authors: Wei Dai, Lixiu Duan, Changfeng Gui, Yuan Li
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the following quasi-linear weighted $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation \begin{equation*}\label{0} -\Delta_N u=|x|^{N\alpha}e^{u}, \qquad x\in \R^N, \end{equation*} where $N \geq 2$. For $\al>0$, by carefully studying the linearized problem and applying the approximation method and bifurcation theory, we prove that, when the parameter $\alpha$ equals to the critical values $\alpha(k):=\frac{\sqrt{k(N-1)(k+N-2)}}{N-1}-1$ for $k \geq 2$, there exist non-radial solutions $u$ (bifurcating from $U_{\alpha(k)}$) to the above quasi-linear H\'enon type Liouville equation such that $u\sim \ln|x|$, $|\nabla u|= O(|x|^{-1})$ at $\infty$ and $\int_{\R^N}|x|^{N\alpha}e^{u}\md x=N\left(\frac{N^2}{N-1}\right)^{N-1}(\alpha+1)^{N-1}\omega_N$. One should note that, $\alpha(k)=k-1$ for $k\geq2$ when $N=2$. Our results successfully extend the existence result of J. Prajapat and G. Tarantello in \cite{PT} concerning the $2$-dimension and Laplacian case (i.e., $N=2$) to the more general $N$-dimension and $N$-Laplacian cases ($N\geq 2$), and extend the results of F. Gladiali, M. Grossi, and S. L. N. Neves in \cite{GGN} and the authors in \cite{DDGL} from $1<p<N$ to the much more complicated limiting case $p=N$. We introduced some new ideas and overcame a series of crucial difficulties, including the nonlinearity nature of the $N$-Laplacian $\Delta_N$, the lack of Green integral representation formula and critical weighted Sobolev embedding inequality, the absence of Kelvin type transforms for linearized/difference equations, the invariance of the total mass under scalings of $u$, and the signs-changing and divergence (to $-\infty$) at $\infty$ of the solutions, which makes the suitable choices of the approximate problems, the (normalized) approximate function sequences and the working space to be quite difficult.

papers.title: A partial answer to Brezis' Open Problem 2.1
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a partial answer to Brezis' Open Problem~2.1, which concerns the uniqueness of solutions to the Ginzburg--Landau equation in the unit disc with the degree-one boundary condition. Let $\lambda_1$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ in the unit disc and set $\varepsilon_*:=\lambda_1^{-1/2}$. We prove that there exists $\delta>0$ such that the radial solution is the unique weak solution for every $\varepsilon\in(\varepsilon_*-\delta,\infty)$. More generally, we establish the analogous uniqueness result for the Ginzburg--Landau system on bounded connected $C^{1,1}$ domains in $\mathbb R^N$, $2\leq N\leq4$, with nontrivial boundary data. In particular, uniqueness persists slightly below the convexity threshold $\varepsilon_*$, where the strict convexity argument is no longer available. The proof combines strict convexity for $\varepsilon\geq\varepsilon_*$ with a compactness argument, nondegeneracy of the solution at $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$ and the implicit function theorem.

papers.title: Inviscid damping without derivatives near Couette flow
papers.abstract:
We study the long-time dynamics near Couette flow for the 2D Euler equations in unbounded geometries. We identify a mechanism of nonlinear inviscid damping at Yudovich regularity, distinct from classical phase mixing: velocity decay driven by spatial evacuation of vorticity.
  The mechanism leads to a geometry-sign classification of the dynamics. In the infinite channel, small nonnegative bounded-vorticity perturbations undergo global damping without derivative assumptions. In the whole plane, small nonnegative perturbations exhibit enhanced dispersion and velocity damping, while non-positive perturbations remain confined and do not damp, even when arbitrarily small in Gevrey classes. Moreover, damping can coexist with infinite-time growth of vorticity derivatives, even under arbitrary shear modulation. The classification is obtained through an interplay between new Lyapunov functionals and Hamiltonian conservation.

papers.title: Explicit diagonalization of the linearized Calder\'on problem on the disk: multiplicity normalization and exponential spectral attenuation
papers.abstract: We study the full angular dependence of the linearized Schr\"odinger form of the Calder\'on problem on the unit disk. We obtain an explicit continuous spectral diagonalization of its normal operator and hence a generalized singular system for the linearized forward map. To our knowledge, this is the first such diagonalization for the full angularly dependent, multiplicity-normalized linearized measurement map on the disk.

papers.title: Isothermal hydrodynamic limit for kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment
papers.abstract:
We study the hydrodynamic limit of kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment and strong local Fokker--Planck forcing. In the limit of small Knudsen number the kinetic densities converge to a local Maxwellian centered around macroscopic quantities satisfying the compressible Euler system with isothermal pressure $p = \s \rho$, while macroscopic alignment is obtained by convolution of the microscopic velocity law with the standard Gaussian, resulting in a different nonlinearity. Such discrepancy has been observed already in \cite{black2025hydrodynamic}.
  In this note we rigorously justify the limit for admissible weak kinetic solutions and non-vacuous limiting macroscopic solution. Our analysis provides a quantitative rate of convergence in terms of relative entropy: $\cH(f_\e | \mu) \lesssim \e$ provided initially $\cH(f_\e(0) | \mu(0)) \leq \e$. In the linear case we recover the known result \cite{karper2015hydrodynamic}.

papers.title: Hessian Estimates for Convex Solutions of Hessian Quotient Equations via Compactness
papers.abstract: We give a compactness proof of interior Hessian estimates for convex solutions of $\sigma_n(D^2u)/\sigma_{n-2}(D^2u)=1$ and $\sigma_n(D^2u)/\sigma_{n-1}(D^2u)=f(x,u,Du)>0$, with $1/f$ concave in the gradient variable in the latter case, revisiting results of Lu and Fung.

papers.title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
papers.abstract: We establish global well-posedness and sharp higher-order decay estimates for the fractional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in $\R^{3}$ with fractional Lam\'e--Navier dissipation $\Lame^\alpha u$ with $\alpha\in[1/2,1]$, and Riesz coupling $\Lambda^{2\beta}\phi=\rho-\bar{\rho}$ with $\beta\in[0,1]$, where $\Lambda:=(-\Delta)^{1/2}$ and $\bar{\rho}>0$ denotes the constant background density. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium in $H^{N\alpha}$ with $N\geq3$ and $N\alpha>5/2$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions. Furthermore, we propagate the negative Sobolev norms with uniform-in-time bounds and derive the higher-order decay estimates, provided that the initial perturbation additionally belongs to $\dot{H}^{-\vartheta}$ for some $\vartheta\in[0,3/2)$. Moreover, we establish the optimality of these decay rates within the prescribed initial data class for the velocity and the Riesz potential in their natural energy norms. The density decay exponents are also optimal whenever the available regularity permits the full Riesz-induced gain. The analysis relies on a nonlinear energy structure adapted to both fractional dissipation and Riesz interaction, together with Sobolev interpolation. The optimality of the decay is proved by constructing smooth initial data localized at low frequencies and proving matching upper and lower decay bounds for the resulting solutions. These solutions show that the low-frequency linear dynamics including the Riesz-induced density gain, persists under nonlinear evolution.

papers.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator on Lipschitz graphs
papers.authors: Joan Hern\'andez, Joan Mateu, Laura Prat
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant. The essential tool is the Coifman--McIntosh--Meyer theorem, applied to a holomorphic family of complex curves, together with the Cauchy integral formula on a contour surrounding the interval of secant slopes. We also include a simpler version of the argument that yields an $O(\log n)$ bound and motivates the choice of contour.

papers.title: A class of sum Hessian quotient equations arising in conformal geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence result of $(n-1)$-admissible solutions to a class of sum Hessian quotient equations with the modified Schouten tensor on Riemannian manifolds. By establishing uniform a priori estimates, we prove the solvability of the problem via degree theory.

papers.title: Training-Induced Escape from Token Clustering in a Mean-Field Formulation of Transformers
papers.authors: Noboru Isobe, Daisuke Inoue, Masaaki Imaizumi
papers.abstract: Transformers perform inference by iteratively transforming token representations across layers. This layerwise computation has been studied empirically, and recent mean-field theories of Transformer dynamics explain how attention can drive token distributions toward clustering. However, existing analyses treat model parameters as prescribed, leaving open how training reshapes this clustering picture. We study this question in a noisy mean-field Transformer in which only a parameter-linear FFN is trained under $L^2$ regularization. We identify a training-induced phase of the inference dynamics across layers: after clustering in the early layers, the token distribution can leave the clustered regime near the final layers. A single gradient-descent update already produces this escape, and minimizers of the training objective satisfy an exponential turnpike bound under which clustering persists through the interior layers. Our analysis is based on an entropy-regularized interaction energy that captures the clustering bias of attention, for which we establish a double-well landscape and a local Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz inequality. More broadly, our results point toward a training-aware mean-field theory in which training and inference dynamics of Transformers are treated together.

papers.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
papers.abstract:
We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class.
  Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.

papers.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
papers.abstract: For $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\beta}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{\beta/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $\beta$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincar\'e and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincar\'e inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincar\'e inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of an optimal control problem for a phase field tumor growth model with hyperbolic relaxation of the chemical potential
papers.authors: Pierluigi Colli, Elisabetta Rocca, J\"urgen Sprekels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal control of a phase field tumor growth model of Cahn--Hilliard type with possibly singular potential in which the often assumed parabolic relaxation of the chemical potential is replaced by a hyperbolic one. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the control problem as the relaxation parameter $\,\alpha\,$ approaches zero. It is shown that the corresponding state and adjoint state variables of the relaxed problem converge in a suitable sense to their counterparts for the unrelaxed regime where $\alpha=0$. Also, weak limits of optimal controls for the relaxed problem can be shown to be optimal controls for the unrelaxed case. Moreover, every fixed optimal control $\,u^*\,$ for the unrelaxed system turns out to be the limit of a family $\{u^*_\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of minimizers of suitable optimal control problems for the relaxed systems, where the original cost functional is replaced by the so-called ``adapted'' cost functional. It is also shown that the variational inequalities satisfied by $u^*_\alpha$, which constitute the first-order necessary optimality conditions of the relaxed problems with adapted cost functional, converge to the corresponding variational inequality fulfilled by $u^*$ for the unrelaxed problem with the original (nonadapted) cost functional.

papers.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
papers.abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.

papers.title: Equivariant localizing motives and multiplicative norms on algebraic K-theory
papers.abstract:
We construct multiplicative norms on equivariant nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory for finite groups $G$. We also construct a genuine equivariant version of THH equipped with a Dennis trace map from K-theory compatible with the multiplicative norms. To do so, we follow the general strategy of Blumberg-Gepner-Tabuada in the nonequivariant case by generalizing their category of localizing motives to the genuine equivariant context, building upon the theory of perfect $G$-stable categories of the first-named author. Crucially, we proceed using the recent perspective on noncommutative motives by the second-named author with Sosnilo and Winges which allows us to deal with non-exact functors on this category of motives. Together with an isotropy separation argument for equivariant cubes, we prove our main theorem that norms of stable categories preserve equivariant motivic equivalences. As an immediate consequence, we obtain a unique equivariant multiplicative refinement of nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory.
  From these constructions and results, we draw several applications, namely: (1) that the endofunctor of (equivariant) tensor powers on ordinary perfect stable categories preserve motivic equivalences; (2) that the multiplicative norms also preserve the additive motivic equivalences, thus yielding a motivic refinement of a result of Elmanto-Haugseng and Cnossen-Haugseng-Lenz-Linskens that connective algebraic K-theory admits multiplicative norms; (3) we construct a genuine equivariant version of topological Hochschild homology equipped with a Dennis trace map that is compatible with multiplicative norms; and (4) we prove that every genuine $G$-spectrum is the K-theory of a perfect $G$-stable category.

papers.title: New examples of non-unique enhancements for triangulated categories
papers.authors: Alice Rizzardo, Julie Symons, Michel Van den Bergh
papers.abstract: We present a general procedure for constructing triangulated categories, linear over a field, with distinct enhancements. Some of our examples can be equipped with a (non-degenerate) t-structure, thereby showing that the existence of a t-structure does not imply uniqueness of enhancements, whether in the strong or weak sense (depending on the example).

papers.title: General Relativity in Three Lines
papers.abstract:
We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Pl\"ucker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Pleba\'nski action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint.
  A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.

papers.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
papers.abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansion of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose mondromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddle points. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package Resurgence.jl

papers.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.

papers.title: Randomness from initial conditions: The challenge of incompleteness
papers.abstract: Certain prima facie deterministic theories, notably Bohmian mechanics and kinetic theory, require ``random'' initial conditions in order to achieve their goals. I analyze recent proposals that this idea should be implemented using algorithmic randomness, seen as a mathematical sharpening of the typicality arguments originally used to understand these theories. On the one hand my analysis includes a critique of these arguments and hence a defense of this sharpening. On the other hand, I argue that Chaitin's incompleteness theorems for random sequences make it impossible for a dynamical theory to either process given random initial conditions beyond some finite (but not arbitrary) number of their digits, or else to state such conditions with arbitrary precision without compromising their randomness (these are two sides of the same coin). This challenges the ability of such theories to make any other predictions than those that hold typically in the usual sense of the word (like macroscopic statements), and moves their alleged determinism high up the metaphysical ladder.

papers.title: Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae
papers.abstract: This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+\Lambda L^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.

papers.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
papers.authors: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera
papers.abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.

papers.title: No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition
papers.abstract: Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nu\~nez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.

papers.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
papers.authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren
papers.abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.

papers.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
papers.authors: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov
papers.abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.

papers.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
papers.abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.

papers.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
papers.abstract: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damk\"ohler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.

papers.title: Parity-dependent sublattice structure of local $2\times2$ correlations in domino tilings of the Aztec diamond
papers.authors: Chaeyeon Kim, Suhwan Yoo, Jeehoon Choi, Hee Young Kwon, Changyeon Won
papers.abstract: We study local $2\times2$ correlations in uniformly random domino tilings of the Aztec diamond $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$, a dimer model with frozen corners and a liquid region bounded by the Arctic circle, and compare them with the square chessboard. For every elementary square the probabilities $P_H$ and $P_V$ of the two coverings by a pair of parallel dominoes satisfy $P_H=P_V=P_1P_2+P_3P_4$, where $P_1,\dots,P_4$ are the probabilities of the four surrounding edges. This known identity, a case of Kuo's graphical condensation, reduces the spatial profile of $P_H$ to single-edge probabilities, which we compute exactly from the inverse Kasteleyn matrix for all squares of $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$. The squares form two interleaved sublattices, distinguished by the color of their lower-left cell. The parity of $n$ decides which sublattice dominates near the center: the one containing the central square for odd $n$, and the other one for even $n$. This sign rule holds for the averaged sublattice contrast for all $4\le n\le22$. It also fixes the location of the global maximum of $P_H$, which lies at or next to the center for odd $n$ and several lattice spacings away for even $n$. Within the central sublattice, the preferred square follows a mod-4 pattern that matches the exactly pinned mean height of the center. On the $L\times L$ chessboard the same rule holds with $n$ replaced by the half-width $L/2$, but the contrast is two to six times weaker, the central edge probability never equals $1/4$, and the maxima of $P_H$ are pinned to the corners. The exact $1/4$ values and the interior, parity-selected maxima are therefore features of the Aztec geometry.

papers.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.

papers.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $\theta_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $\theta_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $\alpha$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
papers.abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.

papers.title: Spinors, Doppelg\"angers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelg\"anger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace

papers.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We find two such types of automorphisms: outer automorphisms exchanging identical current algebra factors, as in Gaiotto's construction, and continuous inner automorphisms generated by the zero modes of spin-one phantom currents. In the latter case, the RG domain walls generically admit a continuous defect conformal manifold. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.

papers.title: Partially isophase electro-magnetic configurations
papers.abstract: Separation of variables in Schr\"{o}dinger equation allows an infinite-dimensional family of physically distinct field configurations that are dynamically indistinguishable in one selected sector, labeled by a conserved quantum number, while differing in all others. We call such a symmetry a partial isophase symmetry. Two main examples are considered: axially symmetric magnetic backgrounds (a rigid spectral flow of the Fock--Darwin oscillator, purely magnetic isophase families, and a two-channel extension) and a Cartesian slab geometry (magnetic barriers in two-dimensional electron gases, treated in the Appendices). We further discuss the consequences of this symmetry for the inverse spectral problem and consider its quasiclassical counterpart.

papers.title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
papers.authors: Hanfeng Zhai, Sh. Akhondzadeh, Ryan B. Sills, Nicolas Bertin, Wei Cai
papers.abstract: We develop a theory for the plastic shear rate $\dot{\gamma}_i$ on each slip system $i$ of face-centered cubic (FCC) single crystals, by integrating the shear rate contributions $\dot{\gamma}_i(l)$ from dislocation links of length $l$. A generalized Orowan equation expresses $\dot{\gamma}_i(l)$ in terms of the link density $n_i(l)$ and the average link velocity $v_i(l)$. This model accurately reproduces the discrete dislocation dynamics (DDD) shear-rate data for all 12 slip systems across 99 loading orientations. In particular, it explains why the plastic shear rate depends exponentially on the resolved shear stress $\tau_i$, as reported previously, in the absence of any thermally activated mechanism. This dependence arises from the exponential tail of $n_i(l)$ filtered through the threshold-like velocity function $v_i(l)$. Furthermore, $v_i(l)$ is well approximated by a single two-dimensional function $v(\tau_i,l)$ for all these slip systems. The link velocity is therefore governed mainly by $\tau_i$ and $l$, with only a minor effect from the complex interactions between slip systems. These interactions instead manifest themselves mainly through $n_i(l)$. As a demonstration of the effect of the link-length distribution on the slip rate, we show that even when $\tau_i$ is limited to a narrow window, the shear rates still span two orders of magnitude. The supply of long links is therefore the dominant factor controlling slip-system activity, outweighing the direct effect of $\tau_i$ on the link velocity.

papers.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
papers.abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

papers.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
papers.abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

papers.title: MIXSim: A multiclass first order traffic model with composition-dependent dynamics for mixed-autonomy urban networks
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel multiclass first order macroscopic traffic model for mixed-autonomy in signalized urban networks, called MIXSim. Human driven vehicles (HDVs) and Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) are represented as separate classes while origin-destination information is retained through commodity specific states. The local vehicle class composition and class specific driving behaviour characteristics determine the parameters of a composition-dependent triangular fundamental diagram. At signalized intersections, the composition of movement demand additionally determines the saturation flow rate, while the realized movement flow is constrained by demand, effective green time, and downstream receiving capacity. Numerical experiments investigate different CAV penetration levels and CAV time gaps, together with alternative signal control strategies. The numerical experiments illustrate how changes in CAV penetration and CAV time gap affect network performance under the tested conditions, and demonstrate the use of MIXSim for comparing signal control strategies across different mixed traffic regimes.

papers.title: Resonance interaction of vector breathers and exotic dynamics in the coupled Hirota equation
papers.abstract: This work presents a systematic theoretical investigation of vector breathers and their nonlinear interactions in the coupled Hirota equation. This model describes the simultaneous propagation of ultrashort optical pulses in optical fibers and contains a key parameter that characterizes the strength of higher-order linear and nonlinear effects, such as third-order dispersion and self-steepening. For the model, we focus on the focusing-focusing case. On a nonzero plane-wave background, we derive explicit expressions for multi-breather solutions of the coupled Hirota equation by the dressing method. For the single-breather solution, by choosing special constant vectors, the vector breathers can be classified into three fundamental types: Type I, Type II, and Type III. We then analyze their characteristic parameters, including spatial localization and group velocity, as well as important special cases such as the Kuznetsov-Ma breathers, Peregrine soliton, and Akhmediev type breathers etc. Through the above analysis, we find that the higher-order effect parameter only modifies the propagation velocity and oscillation period of the breathers, while the resonance conditions remain satisfied: when the wave numbers and frequencies match, inelastic resonant interactions can occur between Type I and Type II breathers, manifesting either as a fusion process (I + II \rightarrow II) or the reverse decay process (III \rightarrow I + II). Furthermore, we present the explicit expression for the two breather solutions of the equation and analyze its rich interaction scenarios, including two breather resonances and elastic collisions, and we point out that the special case of resonance corresponds to the limiting case of merging eigenvalues. Finally, we carry out numerical simulations to verify the accuracy of the obtained solutions.

papers.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
papers.abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincar\'{e} inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region.
