This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.

papers.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.

papers.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
papers.abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.

papers.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard Model in High Dimension
papers.authors: Shahnaz Farhat, Denis P\'erice, S\"oren Petrat
papers.abstract: The Bose-Hubbard model effectively describes bosons on a lattice with on-site interactions and nearest-neighbour hopping, serving as a foundational framework for understanding strong particle interactions and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition. This paper aims to rigorously establish the validity of a mean-field approximation for the dynamics of quantum systems in high dimension, using the Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice as a case study. We prove a trace norm estimate between the one-lattice-site reduced density of the Schr\"odinger dynamics and the mean-field dynamics in the limit of large dimension. Here, the mean-field approximation is in the hopping amplitude and not in the interaction, leading to a very rich and non-trivial mean-field equation. This mean-field equation does not only describe the condensate, as is the case when the mean-field description comes from a large particle number limit averaging out the interaction, but it allows for a phase transition to a Mott insulator since it contains the full non-trivial interaction. Our work is a rigorous justification of a simple case of the highly successful dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for bosons, which somewhat surprisingly yields many qualitatively correct results in three dimensions.

papers.title: Kohn-Sham models for encapsulated two-dimensional materials
papers.abstract: We study Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) models describing the electronic structure of two-dimensional materials placed in a three-dimensional environment, encapsulated between two parallel conducting electrodes. In this geometry, the Dirichlet boundary conditions at the electrodes screen the Coulomb interaction, which becomes effectively short-ranged, of Yukawa type. We prove that some nonlinear Kohn-Sham DFT models are well-posed in this setting, both for periodic materials (such as graphene) and for quasi-periodic materials (such as twisted bilayer graphene and other moir\'e materials for generic incommensurate twist angles).

papers.title: Exact Chained-Word Threshold and Monotone-Path Structure in the Even Root-of-Unity Kaleidoscope Yang-Baxter Algebra
papers.abstract: Qiu, Guan, and Yu conjectured that in the even-order Kaleidoscope Yang--Baxter equation every word $\Lambda T^{k_1}\Lambda\cdots T^{k_M}\Lambda$, built from a square-zero matrix $\Lambda$ and integer powers of a shift $T$ of order $N$, vanishes once $M\geq N/2$. We prove this for every even $N\geq4$ and every complex parameter $u$ with $u\neq0$ and $u^N\neq1$, and show that the bound is sharp. For $M=N/2-1$ we determine exactly which words are nonzero; each of them has rank two. After block reduction, the factors associated with the intervening powers of $T$ lower a common flag of length $N/2$ by at least one step. The spectral idempotents of $T$ then give a presentation of the algebra generated by $T$ and $\Lambda$ by paths between levels, in which two paths compose only when the level changes monotonically. This algebra is independent of $u$, has dimension $N^2-N+2$, and is a pullback of two incidence algebras. Its radical is generated by $\Lambda$ and has nilpotency index $N/2+1$, and the algebra has infinite global dimension and infinite representation type. Replacing powers of $T$ by arbitrary functions of $T$ gives exact rank formulas and, for $N\geq6$, rank-one elements in the top radical power. Finally, four conditions on a filtered pair of operators over an arbitrary field recover the threshold and the radical; none of them can be omitted.

papers.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
papers.abstract: We present a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals from autonomous scattering and reflection data. Spatial homogeneity forces the spectral labels of right- and left-moving particles to be affine with a common slope, so bulk and boundary couplings sample one spectral trajectory. A complete round trip shifts the spectral labels and gives boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations provide local consistency, while boundary-qKZ flatness provides global consistency. We reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by Cayley inversion of the bulk and boundary matching matrices. We apply the construction to rational $SU(N)$ scattering with fundamental boundary impurities and to an $O(3)$ model with a spin-$\tfrac12$ impurity. For the $SU(2)$ impurity, we construct explicit boundary-qKZ solutions as lattice sums of off-shell boundary Bethe vectors and recover the static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes

papers.title: Exponential clustering of bipartite quantum entanglement at arbitrary temperatures
papers.abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects play central roles in the appearance of inexplicable phenomena in low-temperature quantum many-body physics. Such macroscopic quantumness is often evaluated using long-range entanglement, i.e., entanglement in the macroscopic length scale. The long-range entanglement not only characterizes the novel quantum phases but also serves as a critical resource for quantum computation. Thus, the problem that arises is under which conditions can the long-range entanglement be stable even at room temperatures. Here, we show that bi-partite long-range entanglement is unstable at arbitrary temperatures and exponentially decays with distance. Our theorem provides a no-go theorem on the existence of the long-range entanglement. The obtained results are consistent with the existing observations that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures can exist in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations are dominant. In the derivation of our result, we introduce a quantum correlation defined by the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We establish an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems for such a quantum correlation at arbitrary temperatures, which yields our main result by relating quantum correlation to quantum entanglement. As a simple application of our analytical techniques, we derived a general limit on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and the quantum Fisher information, which will attract significant attention in the field of quantum metrology. Our work reveals novel general aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and sheds light on the characterization of long-range entanglement.

papers.title: Singularity and regularity of the critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow
papers.authors: Francesco Caravenna, Rongfeng Sun, Nikos Zygouras
papers.abstract: The Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) provides a natural candidate solution to the ill-posed 2D Stochastic Heat Equation with multiplicative space-time white noise. In this paper, we initiate the investigation of the spatial properties of the SHF. We prove that, as a random measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, it is a.s. singular w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. This is obtained by probing a "quasi-critical" regime and showing the asymptotic log-normality of the mass assigned to vanishing balls, as the disorder strength is sent to zero at a suitable rate, accompanied by similar results for critical 2D directed polymers. We also describe the regularity of the SHF, showing that it is a.s. H\"older $C^{-\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$, implying the absence of atoms, and we establish local convergence to zero in the long time limit.

papers.title: On the pair correlation function of the Sine$_\beta$ process
papers.abstract: We study the Sine$_\beta$ process, the bulk point process scaling limit of beta-ensembles. We provide a representation of its pair correlation function for all $\beta>0$ via a stochastic differential equation, and also via an infinite system of differential equations. We show that the pair correlation function is continuous in $\beta$, and provide estimates for its asymptotic decay. When $\beta=2n$ is an even integer, we characterize the pair correlation function through a linear system of $n$ ordinary differential equations and derive the function's power series expansion. Our results recover the classical explicit formula for the pair correlation function in the $\beta=2$ and $4$ cases. We obtain our results by studying the one-point function of the $\operatorname{HP}_{\beta,\delta}$ process, the point process limit of the circular Jacobi beta-ensemble.

papers.title: The three kinds of three-qubit entanglement
papers.abstract: We construct an important missing piece in the entanglement theory of pure three-qubit states, which is a polynomial measure of W-entanglement. This works in parallel to the three-tangle, which is a polynomial measure of GHZ-entanglement, and to the bipartite concurrence, which is a polynomial measure of bipartite entanglement. We also show that these entanglement measures are ordered, the bipartite measure is larger than the W measure, which is larger than the GHZ measure. It is meaningful then to consider these three types of three-qubit entanglement, which are also ordered, bipartite is weaker than W, which is weaker than GHZ, in parallel to the order of the three kinds of equivalence classes of entangled three-qubit states.

papers.title: Fluid dynamics as intersection problem
papers.abstract:
The main result of the paper is a construction of an infinite-dimensional symplectic manifold, associated with spacetime, its coisotropic submanifold defined as the zero locus of a moment map, and a family of Lagrangian submanifolds determined by the equation of state and the spacetime metric, such that their intersection is precisely the covariant Lichnerowicz--Carter system for a relativistic perfect fluid. On this basis, we clarify the notion of canonical velocity and hydrodynamic invariants, such as the asymptotic Hopf invariant and the Ertel invariant, and obtain a generalization of Kelvin's circulation theorem. We also clarify the relation between the canonical velocity, the four-velocity, and other choices of frames. We point out a five-dimensional origin of the formalism underlying the covariant formulation of hydrodynamics.
  Our formalism extends naturally to fluids with additional degrees of freedom, including multi-component fluids, charged fluids, and superfluids, and incorporates the chiral anomaly and Onsager quantization. It also suggests a direction of research connecting hydrodynamics to Poisson sigma models and topological field theories.
  Furthermore, we argue that a similar approach applies to the theory of self-dual fields, such as chiral bosons in 1+1 dimensions, tensor fields of (2,0) theory in 1+5 dimensions, and the 4-form field of type-IIB supergravity in 1+9 dimensions.

papers.title: Failure of the mean-field Hartree approximation for a bosonic many-body system with non-Hermitian Hamiltonian
papers.authors: Matias Ginzburg, Simone Rademacher, Giacomo De Palma
papers.abstract:
Mean-field Hartree theory is a central tool for reducing many-body dynamics to an effective one-particle evolution. This approximation has been employed when the Hamiltonian governing the many-body dynamics is not Hermitian. Indeed, non-Hermitian Hamiltonians model particle gain/loss or the evolution of open quantum systems between consecutive quantum jumps. Furthermore, the validity of the Hartree approximation for generic non-Hermitian Hamiltonians lies at the basis of a quantum algorithm for nonlinear differential equations. In this work, we show that this approximation can fail.
  First, we consider the most general bosonic mean-field Hamiltonian with two-body interactions and we prove that, for non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, the Hartree equation does not capture the correct second time derivative of the one-particle marginal state at $t=0$ in the thermodynamic limit. Then, we analytically solve a model of $N$ bosonic qubits with a purely anti-Hermitian Hamiltonian, compute the limit for $N\to\infty$ of the one-particle marginal state and show that it does not agree with the solution of the non-Hermitian Hartree equation. We further show that there exists an initial condition such that the exact one-particle marginal state undergoes a finite-time transition to a mixed state, a phenomenon that is completely absent in the case of Hermitian Hamiltonians. Finally, we simulate a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with real spectrum and show that, also in this case, there are initial conditions for which the Hartree equation does not reproduce the correct one-particle marginal state in the limit $N\to\infty$.
  Our findings challenge the validity of the mean-field Hartree approximation for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, and call for additional conditions for the validity of the mean-field regime to model the dynamics of particle gain and loss and the open-system dynamics in bosonic many-body systems.

papers.title: Universality classes, Thermodynamics of Group Entropies, and Black Holes
papers.authors: Henrik Jeldtoft Jensen, Petr Jizba, Piergiulio Tempesta
papers.abstract: Conventional Boltzmann--Gibbs statistical mechanics successfully describes systems with weak to moderate correlations, in which the number of accessible configurations $W(N)$ grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom $N$. However, this framework breaks down for systems for which the effectively occupied configuration space exhibits non-exponential growth. While numerous generalized entropies have been proposed to address this limitation, a coherent link to classical thermodynamic laws has remained elusive. Here, we propose group entropies as a unifying framework, defining universality classes of entropies through the asymptotic scaling of $W(N)$, each yielding an extensive entropy. We show that this approach provides the basis for a consistent thermodynamic formulation beyond the Boltzmann--Gibbs paradigm. In particular, by expressing these entropies in terms of thermodynamic state variables, we demonstrate their consistency with classical thermodynamics, in close analogy to the emergence of the Clausius entropy from the Boltzmann--Gibbs formalism. Focusing on the zeroth thermodynamic law, we identify the empirical temperature and, by using Carath\'{e}odory's formulation of the second law, we derive the associated absolute temperature. As an application, we analyse black-hole thermodynamics using the extensive group entropy class corresponding to stretched-exponential behaviour of $W(N)$ and derive a negative heat capacity, known to be a hallmark property of black holes. This result holds for the stretched-exponential entropies associated with both the Bekenstein--Hawking and Barrow entropy scalings.

papers.title: Hidden symmetry group for particle orbits (timelike geodesics) in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.authors: Stephen C. Anco, Mahdieh Gol Bashmani Moghadam
papers.abstract: For the timelike geodesic equations in Schwarzschild spacetime, three hidden conserved quantities were found recently, which are analogues of dynamical quantities related to the well-known Laplace--Runge--Lenz (LRL) vector in Newtonian gravity. In particular, the geodesic equations possess an LRL angle, an LRL Killing-vector time and an LRL proper time, each of which is a (piecewise) conserved quantity for all timelike geodesics. The present work provides a natural symmetry interpretation for these three quantities by applying Noether's theorem in reverse to the geodesic Lagrangian. This yields three new (hidden) LRL symmetry transformations. Unlike the Killing symmetries, which constitute point transformations on the geodesic configuration variables and close without the use of the geodesic equations, the new symmetries are dynamical transformations which essentially involve the geodesic momenta variables and close only on solutions of the geodesic equations. The commutator structure of the LRL symmetries is shown to depend on whether a geodesic is bounded or not, and horizon-crossing or not, while their physical meaning is connected to their action on the geodesic energy and angular momentum. Together with the Killing symmetries and re-parameterization symmetries of the geodesics Lagrangian, they generate the complete Noether symmetry group of the timelike geodesic equations.

papers.title: Separability from Multipartite Measures
papers.abstract: We show that multi-invariants provide necessary and sufficient criteria for full separability in finite-dimensional multipartite systems. For tripartite three-qubit states, the third-order negativity gives an exact criterion for full separability for both pure and mixed states. We then extend the framework to four-qubit pure states, whose full characterization requires eighteen independent real parameters. We identify eighteen independent entanglement measures, consisting of six bipartite, eight tripartite, and four quadripartite measures, with the third-order negativity serving as a key separability criterion. Finally, we generalize the construction to multipartite qudit systems and discuss an application to conformal field theory.

papers.title: A generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations
papers.abstract: We develop a generalized long-wave limit method for constructing higher-order (degenerate) lump solutions of $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems. Starting from the multi-soliton tau function, we introduce wavenumber rescalings, spectral perturbations, and higher-order phase modulations in a single small parameter, and choose their coefficients so that the lower-order Taylor coefficients vanish. Applying this framework to the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili I equation, we explicitly derive second-order two- and three-lump solutions as well as third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions. The long-time asymptotics of the peak positions and amplitudes describe anomalous scattering of these degenerate lump solutions. Extensions to hybrid higher-order lump solutions associated with multiple distinct spectral parameters are also discussed.

papers.title: Holonomies and Boundary Symmetries in the Discrete BF Formulation of Carroll Dilaton Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct a discrete realization of two-dimensional Carroll dilaton gravity based on a BF-type gauge structure with holonomy variables on lattice links. The bulk theory remains topological, while the physical dynamics is encoded in boundary degrees of freedom. Imposing admissible boundary conditions, we derive the asymptotic symmetry structure directly at the lattice level. The least restrictive conditions yield an affine extension of the Carroll algebra, while additional constraints reduce the symmetry to a conformal sector governed by a discrete Virasoro-type algebra. In the continuum limit, the lattice symmetry structure reproduces the expected affine Carroll algebra together with its conformal reduction. The construction therefore provides the ultra-relativistic counterpart of discrete Jackiw-Teitelboim(JT) gravity.

papers.title: A UV-Finite Refinement of the Ryu-Takayanagi Relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
papers.authors: Philipp Dorau, Albert Much, Leonardo Sangaletti, Rainer Verch
papers.abstract: We establish a refined Ryu--Takayanagi (RT) relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ using \emph{relative entropy} as the central object, in place of the ultraviolet-divergent von Neumann entanglement entropy. Adapting Hollands' exact result for the chiral relative entropy to a diamond region, we express the boundary relative entropy between the vacuum and a coherent state as a Schwarzian functional, which the Fefferman--Graham dictionary identifies with the asymptotic data of a Ba\~nados geometry; the rigidity of three-dimensional gravity promotes this boundary identification to the bulk. To linear order in the metric perturbation, the relative entropy then equals the variation of the RT geodesic length divided by $4G_N$. The construction rests only on the Bisognano--Wichmann/Borchers theorem and the holographic dictionary, giving a UV-finite, operator-algebraic counterpart to the RT relation.

papers.title: Morse Bridge between Planar Kepler and Hyperbolic Landau Dynamics
papers.abstract: A common Morse Hamiltonian bridges the planar Kepler--Coulomb and hyperbolic Landau systems, linking flat electric dynamics to curved magnetic dynamics. A radial Liouville transformation with coupling-constant metamorphosis maps the separated Kepler problem to the Morse system, while fixed-horocyclic-momentum reduction maps the hyperbolic Landau problem to the same system. In a common normalization, the Coulomb coupling is the signed product of the magnetic field and conserved horocyclic momentum, while the quantum Landau reduction has the universal half-density shift $1/4$. Beyond this shared reduction, we construct a direct classical orbit map on the regular nonradial sectors for all signs of the Kepler energy. It maps the Landau height to a scaled inverse Kepler radius, Kepler ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas to magnetic circles, horocycles and hypercycles, and Hamilton's hodograph affinely to the Landau carrier circle. The reduced Kepler symplectic form and the Binet-selected complex structure determine a Poincar\'e K\"ahler metric. Its nondegenerate Binet orbits have constant geodesic curvature of magnitude equal to the inverse eccentricity, while zero coupling gives geodesics. The orbit map identifies this metric isometrically with the Poincar\'e configuration-space metric of the hyperbolic Landau problem. Composing the quantum Liouville maps eliminates the Morse wavefunction and yields an exact weighted intertwining identity between the radial Kepler and horocyclic Landau operator pencils. At distinguished half-integer magnetic fields, the angular-momentum grading of a fixed Kepler shell is reorganized into the finite reduced Landau tower and its threshold endpoint. These exact correspondences hold in the stated reduced sectors despite the unitary inequivalence of the complete parent systems.

papers.title: Bogomol'nyi equations for Kruglov strings
papers.authors: I. Prasetyo, U. Ubaydillah, H. S. Ramadhan
papers.abstract: We construct the Bogomol'nyi equations for Abelian gauge--Higgs vortices in which the Maxwell gauge sector is replaced by Kruglov nonlinear electrodynamics, a power-law family that interpolates between Maxwell theory, Born--Infeld electrodynamics, and exponential electrodynamics, characterized by a dimensionless exponent $\sigma$. Using the stressless method, we derive a pair of first-order equations directly from the vanishing of the spatial stress tensor, without assuming the Higgs potential \textit{a priori}. For generic $\sigma$, the gauge and Higgs sectors are coupled through an implicit algebraic relation. We therefore introduce a constitutive map $\Phi(Y;\sigma)$ and analyze its monotonicity and range to determine the conditions for a smooth admissible Bogomol'nyi branch. For $\sigma>1/2$, the constitutive map is strictly monotonic and unbounded, whereas for $0<\sigma<1/2$ it possesses a finite maximum; the marginal case $\sigma=1/2$ is bounded. These properties yield explicit bounds on the nonlinear parameter $\beta$ for the latter cases. We further obtain closed-form constitutive relations, BPS potentials, and gauge-field equations for six representative values of $\sigma$, spanning linear, quadratic, and cubic algebraic structures. The corresponding vortex profiles are then computed numerically. The resulting BPS string tension is purely topological, $\mu_{\rm BPS}=2\pi n$, independent of both $\sigma$ and $\beta$.

papers.title: Autonomous self-harmonic drift in Langevin dynamics causes a compaction of underlying domain for the density of Stochastic Localization
papers.abstract: Our recent research on Langevin dynamics with self-harmonic drift and classical spins has revealed a strong connection to ``Stochastic Localization," a concept attracting attention in the fields of mathematical geometry and data science. Roughly speaking, the former can be viewed as a version of the latter in which the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space - the domain of the probability distribution function appearing in the latter - is ``compactified'' to the surface of an $n$-dimensional sphere. By comparing the two frameworks, we argue that this compactification is a consequence of requiring the drift to be autonomous. The relationship between the two approaches may expand the scope of Stochastic Localization.

papers.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
papers.abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.

papers.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a non-unital partial symmetric operad (combination restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and replace the construction of the exceptional set by a direct exclusion: we use finite boundary charts for seven of the eight diagrams that can carry an unbounded four-product, and an exhaustive order census for Diagram 5. We derive the necessary mass conditions where needed and show that no germ with an unbounded four-product lies on a curve of normalized central configurations through a positive configuration. Five diagrams are excluded for all complex germs, two on curves through real configurations, and one on curves through positive configurations. Parts of the argument are computer-assisted: exact algebra, interval arithmetic and exact linear programming.

papers.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
papers.abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.

papers.title: Quantitative Volume Estimate on Singular Sets of One-phase Free Boundary Problems in Ricci Limit Spaces
papers.abstract: We study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. We introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. We also introduce a new truncated parabolic Weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. Although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $C\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. Such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of Cheeger and Naber [arXiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $\eta>0$, a $Cr^{n-k-\eta}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. The same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal S_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the Minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal M} \mathcal S_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal H} \mathrm{Sing} \le n-3$ in Chan, Zhang, and Zhu [arXiv:2112.06962] follows. As another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a H\"older manifold structure away from a set of Minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.

papers.title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on simply connected compact rank-one symmetric spaces
papers.authors: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Hui Zhang
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth Riemannian metric on the underlying smooth manifold of a simply connected compact rank-one symmetric space, namely $S^n$ $(n\ge2)$, $\CP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, $\HP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, or $\OP^2$ admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics. Here a prime closed geodesic is a nonconstant closed geodesic which is not an iterate of a shorter one, and geometric distinctness means that the images in the manifold are pairwise different. Thus iterating a geodesic, changing its starting point, or reversing its orientation does not count as a new geodesic. No nondegeneracy assumption on the metric is imposed. These manifolds have bounded loop-space Betti numbers, so the usual homological growth criterion does not yield this conclusion. We use the length filtration together with rotation and reversal of loops. A controlled cut construction gives a uniform filling estimate in the based loop space, with a fixed increase in length independent of degree, which we transfer to free loops. We then calculate global equivariant classes associated with odd and even iterates. Assuming finitely many prime geodesic images forces incompatible requirements at a class's first critical level. The proof treats spheres and projective spaces within a common framework and does not assume a sphere infinitude theorem.

papers.title: Complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that nontrivial complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.

papers.title: Finite Time Noncollapsing K\"ahler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the K\"ahler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact K\"ahler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale.
  We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $\omega(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit.
  Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

papers.title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
papers.abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

papers.title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
papers.authors: Jixiang Fu, Jiuhe Liu, Yunyang Xiao, Shing-Tung Yau
papers.abstract: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Amp\`ere terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature K\"ahler Metrics near the Canonical Class
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any K\"ahler class $[\omega]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2\pi c_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[\omega]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2\pi c_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[\omega]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized K\"ahler--Ricci flow on $X$.

papers.title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
papers.abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

papers.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
papers.authors: Patrick Antweiler, Vicente Cort\'es, Julian Holstein, Markus R\"oser, Aldo Witte
papers.abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

papers.title: Singular Yamabe metrics on complements of closed sets
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq3$ and let $\Lambda\subset \mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at least two points, and satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm H}\Lambda<(n-2)/2$. We prove that there exists a complete metric of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$ on $\mathbb S ^n\setminus\Lambda$, conformal to the round metric.

papers.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $\pi/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $\pi/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijovi\'c, et al. (1999).

papers.title: The Hopf conjecture with $T^3$-symmetry
papers.abstract: We prove that any closed even-dimensional manifold with positive sectional curvature admitting an isometric action by a 3-torus has positive Euler characteristic. We also prove the result for orbifolds.

papers.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
papers.authors: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.

papers.title: Extending Donaldson's HyperK\"ahler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
papers.authors: Christian El Emam, Filippo Mazzoli, Nicholas Rungi, Andrea Seppi, Andrea Tamburelli
papers.abstract: We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperK\"ahler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperK\"ahler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-K\"ahler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.

papers.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.authors: Duong Dinh, Troy Figiel, Joerg Teschner
papers.abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title: Polynomial Maximal Surfaces in H^{2,2} and Spherical Polygons
papers.abstract: We study the moduli space of complete maximal surfaces in pseudo-hyperbolic space $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ with polygonal asymptotic boundary a lightlike $(n+4)$-gon in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, up to the action of $\mathsf{SO}_0(2,3)$. Importantly, this space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ is disconnected for $n\geq 2$. We introduce a \emph{turning invariant} $\Theta$ that classifies the components in terms of the geometry of the boundary polygons in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, which is related to \emph{spherical polygons} in $\mathbb{S}^2$. We provide a geometric parametrization of the moduli space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ via holomorphic data, namely a pair of polynomials $\alpha$, $\beta$. These polynomials appear in relation to certain components of the complexified second fundamental form of the corresponding surface. We then relate the holomorphic data $\alpha,\beta$ with the turning invariant $\Theta$. This leads to characterizations of the \emph{Hitchin component} of polygonal maximal surfaces studied by Tamburelli-Wolf.

papers.title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
papers.abstract: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.

papers.title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
papers.abstract: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $\Delta_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $\Sigma$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $\Sigma$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.

papers.title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
papers.authors: Alejandro Cabrera, David Iglesias Ponte, Juan Carlos Marrero
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.

papers.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
papers.abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.

papers.title: Fixed-spinor radial solutions of a perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation
papers.authors: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang, Yuhang Zhang
papers.abstract:
We study the perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation \[ D_{g_{\mathbb R^n}}\psi
  =
  \frac n2\bigl(1+\varepsilon K(x)\bigr)
  |\psi|^{2^*-2}\psi
  \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^n,\quad n\ge2, \]where $2^*:=2n/(n-1)$, $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $K$ is a prescribed radial function. We establish a finite-dimensional reduction within a radial spinor space determined by a fixed unit spinor, reducing the problem to the analysis of a function of the dilation parameter. Under suitable assumptions on $K$, we obtain explicit existence criteria for solutions with this prescribed spinorial structure, together with a multiplicity criterion yielding solutions associated with distinct scales. These criteria are expressed in terms of the behavior of $K$ at the origin and weighted integral quantities.

papers.title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
papers.authors: Fabius Kr\"amer, Tim Laux, Keisuke Takasao
papers.abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.

papers.title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
papers.authors: Mathias Braun, Nicola Gigli, Robert McCann, Simone Vincini
papers.abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.

papers.title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
papers.abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

papers.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
papers.abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.

papers.title: Equivariant analytic torsion for proper actions
papers.abstract: We construct an equivariant version of Ray-Singer analytic torsion for proper, isometric actions by locally compact groups on Riemannian manifolds, with compact quotients. We obtain results on convergence, metric independence, vanishing for even-dimensional manifolds, a product formula, and a decomposition of classical Ray-Singer analytic torsion as a sum over conjugacy classes of equivariant torsion on universal covers. We do explicit computations for the circle and the line acting on themselves, and for regular elliptic elements of $\operatorname{SO}_0(3,1)$ acting on $3$-dimensional hyperbolic space. Our constructions and results generalise several earlier constructions of equivariant analytic torsion and their properties, most of which apply to finite or compact groups, or to fundamental groups of compact manifolds acting on their universal covers. These earlier versions of equivariant analytic torsion were associated to finite or compact conjugacy classes; we allow noncompact conjugacy classes, under suitable growth conditions.

papers.title: Contact Blow-up Analysis of the Legendrian Mean Curvature Flow and a Smale-type Theorem for Strict Contactomorphisms of Sasakian Spheres
papers.authors: Shu-Cheng Chang, Chin-Tung Wu, Liuyang Zhang
papers.abstract: We study the Legendrian mean curvature flow in $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifolds by parabolic rescalings which preserve the contact structure. In a compact $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifold, regular or not, the contact tangent flows at a Type I singularity are, up to vertical translations of their components, self-similar flows of Legendrian self-shrinkers in the Heisenberg group, and they are unions of Legendrian planes. When the Reeb orbits are not closed, as on the irregular Sasaki--Einstein manifolds, the leaf space of the Reeb foliation is not a K\"ahler manifold or orbifold, and this result does not follow by projecting the flow to a Lagrangian mean curvature flow; its proof combines local transverse estimates with a Gaussian density localised in a flow box of the Reeb foliation. In a regular manifold a Type I singularity can only form at a point of transverse Gaussian density at least $2$. We apply the analysis to strict contactomorphisms $\varphi$ of the standard Sasakian sphere $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, whose Legendrian graphs lie in the $\eta$-Einstein manifold $(\mathbb S^{2k+1}\times\mathbb S^{2k+1})/\mathbb S^1$. The Jacobian of a Legendrian graph obeys a reaction--diffusion equation whose quadratic term is a sum of squares when $k=1$ and is indefinite when $k\geq2$. For every strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^3$, and for every pinched strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, $k\geq2$, the contact blow-ups of the flow of its Legendrian graph are flat, the flow exists for all time and, up to a rotation along the Reeb flow, converges exponentially to the graph of an element of $U(k+1)$. In particular such a $\varphi$ is isotopic to $U(k+1)$ through strict contactomorphisms.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flow with scaling invariant estimates
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove uniqueness for complete non-compact Ricci flow with scaling invariant curvature bound. This generalizes the earlier work of Chen-Zhu, Kotschwar and covers most of the example of Ricci flows with unbounded curvature. In dimension three, we use it to show that complete Ricci flow starting from uniformly non-collapsed, non-negatively curved manifold is unique, extending the strong uniqueness Theorem of Chen. This is based on solving Ricci-harmonic map heat flow in unbounded curvature background.

papers.title: Non-compact Ricci Solitons of Finite Volume with Potential Field of Constant Length
papers.authors: Hemangi Madhusudan Shah, Sharief Deshmukh, Mohammad Aqib
papers.abstract: We study non-compact Ricci solitons of finite volume whose potential vector field has constant length. Under the assumptions that the scalar curvature is constant along the integral curves of the potential field and that a natural divergence term is integrable on the unit tangent bundle, we prove that such Ricci solitons are necessarily trivial. As applications, we characterise $3$-dimensional Ricci solitons of constant length and of finite volume on almost $\alpha$-cosymplectic manifolds. In fact, we show that these spaces are indeed compact quotients of Euclidean spaces. We also study complete, non-compact and finite volume contact metric manifolds in dimension $3$ admitting a Reeb vector field as a Ricci soliton. We show that it is a compact spherical space form. We include some examples to illustrate the necessity of the finite-volume and constant-length assumptions.

papers.title: Eventual Monotonicity of the Willmore Energy under Mean Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We establish the eventual monotonicity of the Willmore deficit \( \int_{\Sigma}H^2\,d\mu-16\pi \) along the mean curvature flow of smooth closed embedded strictly convex surfaces in \( \mathbb R^3 \), thereby complementing Huisken's exponential convergence with an eventual monotonicity property. As a consequence, the Hawking mass is eventually nondecreasing along the contracting mean curvature flow, in contrast with the usual inclusion monotonicity expected of the Hawking mass. We also discuss totally umbilical solutions in three-dimensional space forms, where the monotonicity directions of the Willmore energy and the Hawking mass depend on the sign of the ambient sectional curvature.

papers.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
papers.abstract: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--\'Emery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.

papers.title: On Lorentzian Lie groups of Nonzero Constant Curvature
papers.abstract:
We investigate Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Lorentzian metrics of nonzero constant sectional curvature. We first revisit Heintze's theory and obtain a characterization of the Lie algebras of Riemannian Lie groups of negative constant curvature. We also extend classical results of Nomizu and Barnet to the pseudo-Riemannian setting by constructing a large family of Lie groups carrying incomplete left-invariant metrics of constant sectional curvature.
  We then describe Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature according to the causal nature of their center and derived ideal. This description is complete except when the derived ideal is Lorentzian, for which we obtain a complete classification in dimension four.
  We show that every left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature on \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) is bi-invariant and complete. Moreover, a semisimple Lie group admits a complete left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature if and only if it is locally isomorphic to \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\). We also characterize \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) through the existence of a noncentral spacelike left-invariant Killing vector field. Finally, we classify Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature in dimensions at most four.

papers.title: The interpolation method for the complex Hessian equation on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: In current work, we delve into the study of complex Hessian equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. By imposing a constraint on both the bisectional curvature and the oscillation of the solution, we demonstrate that the Laplacian estimate can be linearly controlled by its gradient estimate. Consequently, we are able to derive gradient estimate for the solution using a standard interpolation argument, without the need to employ the blow-up technique. As an application, we demonstrate that when the right-hand side of the complex Hessian equations approximate 1 in the $L^1$ norm, the desired gradient estimate is obtained.

papers.title: Explicit Ricci-flat Metrics on Kummer K3 Surfaces
papers.authors: Jixiang Fu, Yunyang Xiao, Shing-Tung Yau
papers.abstract: We give a convergent explicit representation of the Ricci-flat K\"ahler metrics supplied by the Calabi--Yau theorem in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed Kummer K3 surface. An explicit radial background has normalized Monge--Amp\`ere residual \(O(a^4)\). Its scalar Green operator \(G_a\) is represented by periodic Ewald kernels, separated radial kernels, finite-dimensional Schur complements, and convergent Neumann series. The coefficients are defined by \(U_{a,1}=-G_af_a\) and \(U_{a,n}=G_a\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}Q_a(U_{a,j},U_{a,n-j})\), where \(Q_a\) is the polarized quadratic Monge--Amp\`ere term. A Green estimate of order \(a^{-1}\) gives a first correction of order \(a^3\) and a convergence parameter of order \(a^2\). A Catalan majorant proves absolute convergence on the entire smooth surface for every sufficiently small fixed \(a\). The sum defines a positive form solving the volume equation; comparison identifies the sum with the smooth normalized Calabi--Yau potential. We also record sufficient analytic conditions for the same recursion on collapsing elliptic K3 surfaces.

papers.title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
papers.authors: A. Cesaroni, M. Novaga, P. Pozzi
papers.abstract: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-H\"older continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.

papers.title: Second Maximum of a Gaussian Random Field and Exact (t-)Spacing test
papers.authors: Jean-Marc Aza\"is, Federico Dalmao, Yohann De Castro
papers.abstract:
In this article, we introduce the novel concept of the second maximum of a Gaussian random field defined on a Riemannian manifold: Once the field reaches its global maximum at a point $t_1$, the second maximum is the largest value of the field away from $t_1$, after the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$ have been removed. This statistic serves as a powerful tool for characterizing the distribution of the global maximum. By employing an ad-hoc Kac-Rice formula, we derive the explicit distribution of the maximum, conditioned on the second maximum and the independent part of the Riemannian Hessian (the part of the Hessian at $t_1$ that is independent of the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$). This approach yields an exact test based on the spacing between these maxima, which we refer to as the spacing test.
  We investigate the applicability of this test for detecting sparse alternatives in Gaussian symmetric tensors, continuous sparse deconvolution, and two-layered neural networks with smooth rectifiers. Theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the calibration and power of the proposed procedures. More generally, we provide a framework for applying the spacing test to continuous sparse regression for any Gaussian random field on a Riemannian manifold.
  Furthermore, when the variance-covariance function is known only up to a scaling factor, we derive an exact Studentized version of the procedure, coined the t-spacing test. We show that this test is perfectly calibrated under the null hypothesis and exhibits high power for detecting sparse alternatives. As a corollary, we derive an exact, non-asymptotic test for the spiked tensor model without requiring prior knowledge of the noise level.

papers.title: Stability of the catenoid for the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature equation in 4 spatial dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish the asymptotic stability of the catenoid, as a nonflat stationary solution to the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature (HVMC) equation in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^{1 + (n + 1)}$ for $n = 4$. Our main result is under a ``codimension-$1$'' assumption on initial perturbation, modulo suitable translation and boost (i.e. modulation), without any symmetry assumptions. In comparison to the $n \geq 5$ case addressed by L\"{u}hrmann-Oh-Shahshahani arxiv:2212.05620, proving catenoid stability in $4$ dimensions shares additional difficulties with its $3$ dimensional analog, namely the slower spatial decay of the catenoid and slower temporal decay of waves. To overcome these difficulties in the $n = 3$ case, the strong Huygens principle, as well as a miraculous cancellation in the source term, plays an important role in arxiv:2409.05968 to obtain strong late time tails. In $n = 4$ dimensions, without these special structural advantages, our novelty is to introduce an appropriate commutator vector field to derive a new hierarchy of estimates with higher $r^p$-weights so that an improved pointwise decay can be established. We expect this to be applicable for proving improved late time tails of other quasilinear wave equations in even dimensions or wave equations with inverse square potential.

papers.title: Large-scale rank and geometry of the Lipschitz metric on geodesic currents
papers.abstract: For a closed orientable surface of genus at least 2, we study the large-scale geometry of the (symmetrized) Lipschitz metric on its space of projective filling geodesic currents. We show that the rank and, hence, asymptotic dimension of the space of filling geodesic currents is infinite. This gives the first example of a natural proper space associated to a closed surface, with a metrically proper isometric action of the mapping class group, that has infinite asymptotic dimension. In contrast, we show that any finite simplex of geodesic currents has rank uniformly bounded above by $8g-9$. We then show a sufficient criterion for its rank and asymptotic dimension to be equal to $8g-9$ and construct examples satisfying it, thus showing the bound is sharp. We further prove that Teichm\"uller space equipped with the Lipschitz metric has rank equal to $3g-3$. In particular, the space of projective filling geodesic currents and the Teichm\"uller space are not quasi-isometric.

papers.title: Napoleonic triangles on the sphere from similar chord triangles
papers.abstract: We study a variant of Napoleon's construction on the unit sphere, in which the triangles erected on the sides of a spherical triangle $ABC$ are required to have similar isosceles chord triangles with apex angle $\beta\in(0,\pi/2)$. For a non-equilateral $ABC$, we prove that the triangle $XYZ$ of spherical circumcentres is equilateral if and only if $\cos(\theta_a+\theta_b+\theta_c\pm\Omega/2)=0$, where $\theta_a,\theta_b,\theta_c$ are the base angles of the isosceles spherical triangles $XBC$, $YCA$, $ZAB$, $\Omega$ is the area of $ABC$, and the sign $+$ (resp.~$-$) corresponds to the outward (resp.~inward) construction. We derive from this an explicit classification in terms of two quadrics and a cubic inequality. It recovers the theorem of Dipierro, Noakes and Valdinoci for $\beta=\pi/3$, and exhibits three families of solutions for $\beta>\pi/3$, together with a fourth one when $\cos\beta<1/4$.

papers.title: On the Solution Sets of the Cone-Volume Map
papers.authors: Tom Baumbach, Zhang Chen, Martin Henk
papers.abstract: For a fixed set $U=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ of outer unit normals, we consider the cone-volume map which associates to a vector of support numbers $b\in\mathbb R^m_{> 0}$ the cone-volume vector $\gamma\in\mathbb R^m$ of the polytope \[ P(U,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:U^\top x\leq b\}. \] We study its fibers $S(U,\gamma)$ over prescribed cone-volume vectors $\gamma$, with particular emphasis on finiteness and non-uniqueness. We give characterizations of the irreducibility of $U$ in terms of properties of the cone-volume map and its solution sets. In particular, for irreducible $U$, we show that $S(U,\gamma)$ is finite for all $\gamma$ outside a set of measure zero in the cone-volume cone, and we give an explicit upper bound for its cardinality. In the planar case, we prove that $S(U,\gamma)$ has semialgebraic dimension at most one for arbitrary $U$. Moreover, for every $U\in\mathcal{U}(2,m)$ with $m\geq 4$, there exists a cone-volume vector $\gamma$ for which $S(U,\gamma)$ contains at least two distinct elements. As a consequence, there exist two distinct smooth planar convex bodies with the same cone-volume measure. Finally, for $U$ in general position, we show that the number of solutions is odd for every cone-volume vector outside the exceptional set.

papers.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.

papers.title: The Rate of the Delsarte Bound for Binary Codes and Spheres
papers.abstract:
We give the asymptotic rate of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes. This extends previous work of the author which formulated and proved an analogue of the conjecture of Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini for binary codes, obtaining the rate of the Delsarte linear program at distance $1/2-1/\pi$.
  The lower bounds introduce ideas from potential theory into the study of Delsarte's bounds, whereby the measures underlying a system of orthogonal polynomials give an obstacle problem. We solve the resulting obstacle problem in the case of binary codes and spherical codes, obtaining a closed form for the lower bound in terms of elliptic integrals. For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.
